implementerProof.how: Round 7: I drove the collector's namespace separation through the real `session_copy` with the collector's own directories present rather than reading the layout; I re-ran both halves of its negative controls and went past its count by mutating one guard at a time, which attributes each control to the guard it pins; I classified its `envoy-go` claim from the run's own log and the branch's envoy footprint rather than accepting the report; and I drove the claim guard at `CheckPod` rather than reading `legionClaim`. Rounds 1 to 6 were each verified as those rounds record.

proof.criterion: No name a pod chooses can reach a path the transcript collector owns.
proof.surface: The real `session_copy` extracted from `scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh` at this head, writing into `transcripts/pods` as `collect_transcripts` now does, with `transcripts/controller` and `transcripts/daemon-controller` already present and the first holding a file.
proof.command: Seed keys deriving `controller`, `daemon-controller`, `pods`, a `../escape.jsonl` remainder and a nested `controller/nested.jsonl`; run `session_copy` into `transcripts/pods`; walk the whole `transcripts` tree
proof.observed: Every derived name lands inside `transcripts/pods/` — `controller`, `daemon-controller`, `pods`, `.._escape.jsonl`, `controller_nested.jsonl` — and `transcripts/controller/keep.jsonl` is byte-unchanged. The class is closed by the destination rather than by reserved names: the traversal guard requires each written name to resolve as a direct child of the copy's own directory, and that directory is now the collector's sibling, so no name can leave it.
proof.negativeControl: The collector's own file, placed before the run and read after it: had any derived name reached a collector path, that file or its directory would have changed. Neither did.

proof.criterion: The unchecked-write class in the collector, and the sensitivity of the controls that pin it.
proof.surface: The script at this head, read for the class, and `bun test scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-session-text.test.ts` run against copies of the script with one guard disabled at a time.
proof.command: Read `record_pair` whole; then run the control suite unmodified, and again with the collision arm, the empty/dot name arm and the traversal arm each disabled in turn in a copy
proof.observed: Every write in `record_pair` is guarded — `mkdir -p`, `printf > reviewer.jsonl`, `pair_dispatch > $agent.json`, `printf > session-stem`, each `|| return 1`, with `session_copy` already returning non-zero — and there is no fifth write in the function. The suite is 33 pass / 0 fail unmodified. Disabling the collision arm fails 6 controls, the name arm 1, the traversal arm 1: the author's 8 against 25, now attributed guard-by-guard, so every control pins a guard and every guard has at least one control.
proof.negativeControl: The mutations are the control: a suite that passed under all three would pin nothing. One of them nearly escaped me — my first attempt at the traversal mutation used an anchor that did not match, so it changed nothing and the suite passed, which reads exactly like a guard no test cares about. I verified the mutation had landed before trusting the result.
proof.doesNotSettle: The class is closed in `record_pair` and not in the file: `production_audit`'s `printf … >"$evidence/run-sessions.json"` (`:2669`) is the same shape — an unguarded write inside a function whose failure is checked, with errexit off inside it — so the write failing leaves the audit passing with its evidence missing. Pre-existing and outside this change's diff; named rather than folded into a clean report.

observations: Three times today a step of my own silently did nothing and its result read like a finding: `od` collapsing repeated lines to `*` (an odd-length hex that looked like corruption), a string replacement whose anchor did not match (a mutation that changed nothing and read as a guard no test pins), and an out-of-tree copy one head stale (a guard that looked unimplemented and was not). Each was caught before it was reported, by checking that the step had landed rather than that its output looked plausible. The remedy is the same in all three and is worth a line in the retro note beside `skipped` is a third answer: verify the instrument changed what it claims to change, then read what it says.
notReachedHere: The seven inverted Stage 4a per-check assertions are unrun, not passing, and Stage 4b has run at no head. Unchanged and unchangeable from here.
Nothing this round touched the cluster: the drain of nineteen trees was still running.
residualRisks: Unchanged from round 5: the single generation counter behind the gap record; a daemon restarting inside the replacement's gap; and the stable claim name meaning a replacement pod waits on its predecessor's claim being reaped.

The transcript collector copies what it can and fails the run. A run that failed with most evidence kept and a run that passed with evidence missing look alike in the directory and differ in the verdict line; the verdict line is now the one that moves.
